title: Opposition Protests TMC Rebel Invite at Monsoon Session All-Party Meet
excerpt: A symbolic walkout by opposition parties over the government's invitation to a breakaway TMC faction sets the stage for a combative Monsoon Session, with NEET paper leaks and Ayodhya temple donation controversies also on the agenda.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Opposition parties staged a walkout protesting the government's invitation to a rebel TMC faction.
  • The walkout united the INDIA bloc, including previously absent DMK and AAP members.
  • The rebel TMC faction seeks separate parliamentary recognition, pending Speaker's decision.
  • The Monsoon Session will address NEET paper leaks and Ayodhya temple donation controversies.
Opposition's Symbolic Walkout
›Opposition walkout on July 19, 2023.
›Protest against rebel TMC faction's invitation.
›INDIA bloc members united, including DMK and AAP.
›Rebel TMC faction led by Sudip Bandyopadhyay and Dr Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar.
  • Opposition parties staged a symbolic walkout from the customary all-party meeting on July 19, protesting the government's invitation to the 20-member rebel TMC faction that has aligned with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI).
  • The walkout united the INDIA bloc, with Congress's Jairam Ramesh noting that even the DMK and AAP — which have not been attending recent bloc meetings — joined the protest.
  • The rebel TMC faction, led by Sudip Bandyopadhyay and Dr Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, has sought separate recognition as a parliamentary group, but a decision remains pending with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.
  • The Monsoon Session, running from July 20 to August 13, is expected to be contentious, with opposition plans to raise the NEET-UG paper leak, alleged irregularities in Ayodhya Ram Temple donations, and foreign policy questions.

India's opposition parties staged a coordinated walkout from the all-party meeting convened ahead of Parliament's Monsoon Session on Sunday, firing the opening salvo in what promises to be one of the most contentious parliamentary sessions in recent memory. The immediate trigger: the Modi government's decision to invite leaders of a breakaway Trinamool Congress faction to the discussions.

The meeting, chaired by Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju at the Parliament House Annexe in New Delhi, was held a day before the Monsoon Session officially begins on July 20. Opposition leaders argued that inviting the rebel TMC group amounted to recognising a faction whose request for separate parliamentary status is still pending before Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla.

The TMC Split at the Centre of the Storm

In June, a group of 20 TMC lawmakers informed Speaker Birla that they had merged with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) and wished to sit in the House as a separate bloc. The faction is led by veteran TMC leaders Sudip Bandyopadhyay and Dr Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, and has extended support to the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance.

""The Speaker will take a decision on those petitions."

""The Speaker will take a decision on those petitions."

While the Speaker has ordered separate seating arrangements for the rebel MPs, a formal decision on the merger remains pending. The opposition contends that the government's invitation to these leaders pre-empts the Speaker's ruling.

"All opposition parties staged a walkout from the all-party meeting for a few minutes. This was a mark of protest against the decision of the Modi government to invite the NCPI that is a parking place for 20 so-called 'rebel' TMC MPs when a final decision is still pending with the Speaker," said Congress MP Jairam Ramesh.

A Rare Show of Opposition Unity

Perhaps more significant than the walkout itself was the breadth of participation. Ramesh noted that the DMK and AAP — both of which have been absent from recent INDIA bloc coordination meetings — joined Sunday's protest, signalling a tactical reunification of the opposition on parliamentary floor strategy even as broader coalition politics remain fractured.

Samajwadi Party MP Dharmendra Yadav reinforced the message, saying the entire opposition is united "no matter how much the government tries to engineer defections or create divisions." CPI(M) Rajya Sabha member John Brittas said the opposition walked out because "the sanctity of the all-party meeting has been sullied."

The TMC's own leadership has distanced itself from the rebels. Party MP Saugata Roy dismissed the split as irrelevant to parliamentary discussions, noting that the TMC has filed disqualification petitions against the defecting legislators. "The Speaker will take a decision on those petitions. Our concern is not to discuss this issue," Roy said.

Contentious Monsoon Session Ahead
›Monsoon Session: July 20 - August 13, 2023.
›Five new bills to be introduced.
›Key issues: NEET paper leak and Ayodhya temple donations.
›Opposition plans to challenge government on multiple fronts.

The Broader Legislative Battleground

The Monsoon Session, scheduled to run from July 20 to August 13, carries a packed and politically charged agenda. The government plans to introduce five new bills, including amendments to the Income-Tax Act, the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, the Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, and the MSME Development Act. The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, introduced in March, will also be taken up for passage.

Notably absent from the legislative agenda is the Delimitation Bill — the package of two Constitutional Amendment Bills that proposed raising the Lok Sabha's maximum strength from 550 to 850 seats. The government failed to secure the required two-thirds majority during the April special session, and sources say the package may be reconsidered after fresh Union Cabinet approval.

NEET and Ram Temple on Opposition's Radar

Beyond the TMC controversy, the opposition has signalled it will aggressively target the government on two high-profile issues. The NEET-UG 2026 paper leak — the latest in a string of examination integrity scandals — is expected to dominate Question Hour and adjournment motions. Opposition parties have also flagged alleged irregularities in the handling of devotee donations at Ayodhya's Ram Temple, with Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Priyanka Chaturvedi demanding a parliamentary discussion on what the opposition calls the "theft" of temple funds.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh has said the party will strongly oppose the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill and any move to reintroduce the delimitation package, while also pressing for accountability on Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's comments regarding Operation Sindoor casualties.

What's Next

Sunday's walkout was symbolic — opposition leaders returned to the meeting room after a few minutes — but it sets the tone for the weeks ahead. With the TMC rebellion reshaping parliamentary arithmetic, the delimitation question lingering in the background, and multiple controversies providing ammunition, the Monsoon Session is likely to see more confrontation than legislation. The first real test comes on Monday, when both Houses convene and the opposition is expected to meet separately to finalise a unified floor strategy.

nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora watching parliamentary politics closely, the TMC rebellion and opposition unity dynamics will shape the political landscape heading into the 2029 general elections. Legislative outcomes on education reform and the delimitation question also carry implications for representation and governance in their home states.
